explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/947: there is no exact covering system, i.e. no finite family of congruence classes a_i (mod n_i) with distinct n_i such that every integer lies in exactly one class (Mirsky–Newman, Davenport–Rado). The Lean statement ¬ ∃ c : StrictCoveringSystem ℤ with pairwise disjoint cosets: a StrictCoveringSystem is a finite family of cosets a_i + I_i covering ℤ with ideals I_i ≠ ⊥, ⊤ (moduli n_i ≥ 2) and injective moduli (distinct n_i); covering plus pairwise disjointness is exactly 'every integer in exactly one class'. Excluding modulus 1 rules out the trivial system {0 mod 1}, as the docstring notes, and modulus 0 classes are singletons that cannot be part of a nontrivial example anyway. Faithful.
